title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook: Communications, Templates, and Runbooks
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates the incident process, runbook templates, postmortem guidance, on-call rotation rules, game day plans, and standard status page / customer communications templates used by Redwood Inference. It is intended for on-call engineers, SREs, support, and engineering managers who participate in incident response.

Goals:
- Ensure fast detection and mitigation of customer-impacting events.
- Standardize communications to internal stakeholders and customers.
- Provide repeatable runbooks and postmortem practice to reduce recurrence.

Severity definitions

1) Sev 0 (Emergency): platform-wide outage or data-loss affecting all customers or critical security incident.
2) Sev 1 (High): major customer-facing degradation (e.g., >25% of requests failing, model-serving outage for a major region).
3) Sev 2 (Medium): partial degradation affecting a subset of customers or functionality (e.g., intermittently elevated latencies, single-worker pool degradation).
4) Sev 3 (Low): minor impact, best-effort degradation, or operational maintenance items.

Alert thresholds and typical pager routing

- Sev 0: Control-plane down, data loss — Pager + Slack #oncall-critical — SLA ack: 2 minutes — Primary responder: On-call SRE & Eng Lead — Escalation window: 2 minutes.
- Sev 1: Regional model serving failures >25% — Pager — SLA ack: 5 minutes — Primary responder: On-call service owner — Escalation: 10 minutes.
- Sev 2: Elevated p95 latency > threshold — Pager (optional) — SLA ack: 15 minutes — Primary responder: Service owner on-call — Escalation: 30 minutes.
- Sev 3: Non-critical errors / degraded metrics — Slack / ticket — SLA ack: 24 hours — Primary responder: Team triage — Escalation: 48 hours.

On-call rotations and responsibilities

- Primary on-call: first responder for alerts tied to a specific service (24/7 rotation, typical shift = 1 week).
- Secondary on-call: backup who covers escalations and handles handoffs; responsible for paged escalations if primary does not respond.
- SRE/Platform on-call: owns cross-service mitigations, runbook maintenance, cluster-level actions.
- Incident Commander (IC): appointed for Sev 0/Sev 1 incidents to coordinate response, comms, and triage.

Rotation rules:
1. Shift length: default 1 week (Mon 08:00 - Mon 08:00 UTC). For teams with high-frequency alerts, consider 3-4 day shifts.
2. Handoffs: Mandatory handoff doc posted to #oncall-handoffs Slack channel with active incidents, outstanding tasks, and known degradations.
3. Time off and substitutions: Use the on-call scheduling tool to assign coverage 2+ weeks ahead; escalate to manager if coverage gaps occur.
4. Compensation / recognition: follow company policy in company-handbook/03_benefits-and-perks for on-call pay.

Incident lifecycle: step-by-step procedure

1) Detection & Triage
- Alert triggers; on-call acknowledges in paging tool within SLA.
- Triage: identify impacted service, scope (users, regions), and likely failure domain.
- If Sev1/Sev0, immediately notify IC and SRE lead.

2) Mitigation
- Apply the relevant runbook (see Runbook Templates below).
- If no runbook exists, follow the temporary mitigation checklist:
  1. Isolate the faulty component (drain nodes, stop rollout).
  2. Roll back recent deploys if correlation exists.
  3. Switch traffic to healthy region or fallback model variant.
  4. Increase autoscaling temporarily if capacity constraint.

3) Communications
- Internal: IC posts initial incident summary to #incidents Slack channel within 15 minutes for Sev 1/0. Update every 30 minutes until mitigation.
- Status page: Publish incident notice (see Status Page templates). For Sev 1/0, create/update a status page incident within 15 minutes.
- Customer comms: Follow customer comms templates (see section). Use legal/compliance for regulated customers.

4) Recovery & Verification
- Confirm system metrics returned to baseline for at least two consecutive evaluation windows (typical window = 5 minutes).
- Verify no data loss and perform smoke tests for representative customer flows.

5) Post-incident
- IC assigns postmortem lead within 48 hours.
- Complete postmortem draft within 5 business days. Publish final postmortem and remediation plan within 10 business days.

Runbook templates (standardized sections)

Each runbook must include the following flat sections (use as checklist):
- Title (service/component)
- Owner (on-call rotation name and pager)
- Pager playbook (how to acknowledge, silence, escalate)
- Symptoms: metrics and logs that indicate this failure
- Initial triage steps (quick checklist)
- Known mitigations with exact commands/API calls
- Rollback steps (if applicable)
- Smoke tests / verification steps
- Post-incident follow-ups and owners

Example runbook excerpt:

Title: model-serving-pool-oom
Owner: model-serving-team on-call (pager: +1-555-0100)
Symptoms:
- Increased OOM crash count on node pool model-serving-pool-3
- p50/p95 latency spikes and increased 5xx errors
Initial triage steps:
1. Check node-level OOM logs: `kubectl -n inference logs -l pool=model-serving-pool-3 --tail 200`
2. Check pod restarts and recent deploys: `kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide --selector=pool=model-serving-pool-3`
Quick mitigations:
- Increase node pool capacity: `gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize model-serving-pool-3 --size=10`
- Temporarily reduce batch size by updating config map and rolling restart on one replica to validate
Verification:
- Confirm 5xx rate drops to <1% and p95 latency returns within 20% of baseline for two windows.

Postmortem template (required fields)

- Title
- Incident ID (e.g., INC-2026-000123)
- Severity
- Timeline (UTC) - concise ordered bullets with timestamps
- Impact (customers affected, regions, estimated downtime)
- Root cause analysis (clear causal chain)
- Remediation & action items (owner + due date)
- Mitigations in response and why they worked/did not work
- CIAs / Lessons learned
- Prevention plan / follow-ups
- Link to relevant runbooks, dashboards, PRs

Game day & exercises

- Quarterly game days: run a 2-hour simulated incident (Sev 1 scenario) per team per quarter.
- Objectives: validate runbooks, measure mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to recover (MTTR), practice comms.
- Roles assigned in game day: IC, Communications lead, Technical lead, Scribe (for timeline), Customer comms lead.
- After action: publish a short AAR (after action report) within 3 business days and update runbooks.

Status page and customer communications templates

Status page incident fields (minimum):
- Title (short)
- Status (investigating, identified, watching, resolved)
- Impact (concise customer-facing summary)
- Regions affected
- Start time (UTC)
- Updates (timestamped bullets)
- Root cause (post-resolve)
- Next steps / mitigation actions in progress

Customer email / support template (for high-impact incidents)

Subject: [Redwood] Service disruption affecting inference API - {Short impact summary}

Body:
Hello {Customer Name},

We are investigating a service disruption affecting the Redwood inference API. Summary: {one-line summary}. Impact: {list of affected regions/features}. Start time: {UTC timestamp}.

What we're doing: {bulleted mitigation actions}.
Estimated next update: {UTC timestamp}.

We will follow up with a full incident report once available. If you require an urgent call, reply to this message and your account team will arrange it.

Sincerely,
The Redwood Incident Response Team

Internal incident update template (Slack pinned message):
- Incident ID: {INC-YYYY-NNNN}
- Severity: {Sev}
- Start time: {UTC timestamp}
- Short summary: {one-line}
- Current status: {investigating / identified / mitigated / resolved}
- Owner(s): {IC, Tech Lead, Scribe}
- Next update: {UTC timestamp}

Communication cadence recommendations

- Sev 0/1: internal updates every 15-30 minutes until mitigated; customer-facing status updates every 30 minutes or on substantive changes.
- Sev 2: internal updates every 60 minutes; customer update within 4 hours if customers impacted.
- Sev 3: update as part of normal triage cycle.

Post-incident follow-up and tracking

- Postmortem owner is responsible for tracking action items in the team's backlog. Each action item must have an owner and due date.
- Track remediation completion in the SRE board and link PRs/changes to the postmortem.
- Runbook updates: update runbook within 5 business days after incident and add "last-tested" date.

Appendix: quick-reference commands and dashboards

- Common dashboards: `infra/inference-overview`, `model-serving/pool-health`, `api/errors-by-code`
- Useful alerts to check: 5xx-rate, p95-latency, instance-restart-rate, kv-cache-miss-rate
- Contact matrix: oncall+sre@redwood.internal (SRE rotation), support@redwood.com (customer-facing), security@redwood.com (security incidents).
content_summary: Consolidated playbook for incident process, runbooks, postmortems, rotations, game days, and comms templates with examples and templates
